title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (v17)
author: Aisha Patel
summary: A single reference that combines the product overview, technical requirements, design notes, roadmap milestones, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference v17.
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Product Requirements (PRD), design specifications, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging notes, and the release notes for Unified Inference v17. Intended audience: product managers, engineering leads (runtime, infra, platform), solutions and sales, and customer success.

Background and problem statement:
- Customers need a consistent, predictable inference experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Key pain points: unpredictable token cost, inconsistent latency at scale, and friction when migrating model versions between deployment modes.
- v17 focuses on tightening performance SLAs, simplifying packaging, and introducing pricing constructs that align to predictable unit economics for mid-market and enterprise customers.

Goals (measurable):
1. Reduce median 99th-percentile latency for text generation by 15% across standard workloads (sequence length <= 1024).
2. Improve serving cost-efficiency for customer workloads by 20% through smarter batching + cache hints and suggested quantization profiles.
3. Increase Dedicated conversion rate by 25% from high-usage hosted accounts via new reserved capacity bundles.
4. Ship a clear, simpler pricing tier that maps to Hosted, Dedicated (committed), and Private (license + support) by the end of Q4 2027.

Non-goals:
- v17 will not introduce new core model training capabilities.
- No major UI redesign of the Console; UX polish only.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Latency: median and p99 measured per model class and route. Target: p99 reduction >= 15%.
- Cost: tokens-per-dollar improvements measured via A/B experiments. Target: 20% uplift for qualifying workloads.
- Adoption: number of Hosted customers on recommended pricing bundles who then convert to Dedicated within 90 days. Target: 25% increase.
- Quality regressions: < 1% of eval regression alerts per week attributable to runtime changes.

Requirements (high-level):
- MUST: Unified API parity across all deployment modes for text generation, chat, embeddings, and tool/function calling.
- MUST: Streaming support and function-calling preserved for all public SDKs.
- MUST: Runtime path optimizations (kernel selection, continuous batching) exposed to autoscaling policies.
- SHOULD: Offer a recommended quantization profile per model class (FP16, int8-quantized variants) surfaced in model catalog.
- SHOULD: Add caching hints API so customers can opt-in to prefix/KV caching for conversational workloads.
- MAY: Introduce a beta of model-level cost caps for Hosted customers.

Detailed acceptance criteria (examples):
1. API parity validation: test harness shows identical output shape and streaming behavior across hosted and dedicated deployments for the same model variant and prompt set.
2. Latency improvements: benchmarking suite (benchmarking-and-perf-suite) shows p99 median reduced by 15% on x1-standard workload across top 10 customer models.
3. Pricing bundles: Billing UI and API return expected price tiers and commitment discounts for Dedicated bundles; documented in pricing-and-packaging.

Design specifications (overview):
- High-level architecture:
  - Control plane (managed) remains the orchestrator for model catalog, rollout policies, observability hooks, and billing.
  - Data plane runtime improvements in v17:
    - Kernel selector: enhanced heuristics that choose kernels by model family, sequence length histogram, and batch-size distribution.
    - Smart batching: adaptive timeout + size-based batching with workload-aware thresholds per route.
    - KV/prefix cache: optional checkpoint-aware cache with TTL and evictions policy. Cache hints API allows route-level annotation: {cache: true, key_prefix: session_id}.
  - Smart routing: policy layer supports cost-first and latency-first routing, with automatic fallback to compatible model variants if a route is constrained.

- API contract changes (backwards-compatible):
  - New optional parameter: cache_hint (object) — accepts mode: [off|session|prefix], ttl_seconds, and scope: [route|customer]. Default: off.
  - Billing metadata returned in response headers: X-RW-Model-Version, X-RW-Effective-UnitCost. These are optional and flagged behind feature flag for early adopters.

- Console integration:
  - Per-route recommendations card (redwood-optimize) that suggests batching configs and quantization profiles.
  - Pricing preview when creating Dedicated reservations that projects cost based on baseline throughput and historical usage.

Roadmap and themes (quarterly milestones):
- Q3 2027 (in-flight): Kernel selector v1, smart-batching flags, beta cache hints API, pricing bundle design complete.
- Q4 2027: GA Kernel selector, smart-batching enabled by default for new routes, Dedicated reservation bundles launch, pricing tier rollout (Hosted Standard / Hosted Pro / Dedicated Reserved / Private License).
- Q1 2028: Console recommendations expanded, model-level cost caps beta, partnership integrations for on-prem packaging.

Roadmap table:
| Quarter | Milestone | Owner | Success criteria |
| Q3 2027 | Kernel selector v1 + batching flags | eng-serving-runtime | Benchmarks show p95 reduction >= 10% |
| Q4 2027 | Dedicated reservation bundles GA + pricing tier launch | product + finance | Sales conversion + billing validation |
| Q1 2028 | Cost caps beta + Console recommendations | eng-platform + product | Beta customers onboarded (10 accounts) |

Pricing and packaging notes (summary):
- Pricing goals: Transparency, predictability, and alignment to customer unit economics. Pricing must be easy to estimate from usage and provide clear incentives for efficient serving (batching, caching, quantization).

Proposed pricing tiers (high-level):
1) Hosted Standard (pay-as-you-go)
  - Use-case: low-volume developers, early-stage startups.
  - Billing model: per-token + small per-request overhead. No commitments.
2) Hosted Pro
  - Use-case: growing teams with predictable traffic but not ready for Dedicated.
  - Billing model: discounted per-token rates, monthly quota, priority routing.
3) Dedicated Reserved
  - Use-case: production teams requiring predictable latency and throughput.
  - Billing model: monthly/annual commitments for GPU pools (slots), committed throughput units, with burst capacity priced separately. Includes SLA.
4) Private (VPC / on-prem)
  - Use-case: regulated customers and those requiring air-gapped deployments.
  - Billing model: license fee + deployment support + optional managed updates and observability add-on.

Pricing table (representative example):
| Tier | Per-token USD | Commitment | Notes |
| Hosted Standard | $0.0009 / 1k tokens | None | Basic support |
| Hosted Pro | $0.0006 / 1k tokens | Monthly quota | Priority routing |
| Dedicated Reserved | Custom | Annual/Monthly | Includes capacity, SLA |
| Private | Custom | Contract | License + Support |

Packaging guidance for sales and solutions:
- Provide a quick calculator for customers: projected tokens/day x expected response lengths x concurrency -> suggested tier and savings for Dedicated.
- For Dedicated proposals include: expected GPU families, baseline throughput (tokens/s), SLA terms (99.9% uptime), RTO/RPO for upgrades.

Rollout plan and operational checklist:
1. Feature flags and progressive rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
2. Monitoring: add dashboards for kernel selection distribution, batching efficiency, cache hit rates, and per-route effective unit cost.
3. Evals: run comparative evals before enabling default batching heuristics to detect quality regressions.
4. Customer communication: release notes, migration guide, and webinars for Dedicated bundle changes.

Release notes (v17.0.0) — 2027-10-01:
- GA: Kernel selector (v1) that improves p95/p99 latency for many conversational models.
- GA: Dedicated reservation bundles launched with new billing metadata in API.
- Beta: Cache hints API (opt-in).
- Console: Pricing preview for Dedicated reservations and per-route optimization suggestions (experimental).
- Bug fixes: Reduced cold-start penalty for small requests, fixed edge-case in streaming chunk ordering for function-calls.

Known issues and mitigations:
- Some third-party model variants show slight perturbations when aggressive quantization profiles are applied. Mitigation: default to conservative quantization and surface explicit test harness for customers.
- Billing metadata behind flag; early adopters may see missing headers in some Dedicated edge cases. Monitoring ticket: BILL-2648.

Appendix: Example API usage (node.js)

// Node.js example: streaming generation with cache_hint
const response = await redwood.generate({
  model: 'rw-unified-13b',
  prompt: 'Summarize the following customer support thread',
  max_tokens: 256,
  stream: true,
  cache_hint: { mode: 'session', ttl_seconds: 3600, scope: 'route' }
});

Notes on evaluation and backward compatibility:
- All API changes are additive and behind feature flags where appropriate. Backcompat tests are part of the CI gating (ci-cd-and-build).
- Regression thresholds are defined in applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails.

Next steps:
- Complete Dedicated bundle pricing finalization with finance by 2027-10-15.
- Ramp canary for smart-batching to 25% traffic by 2027-10-20.
- Publish customer migration guide and pricing calculator by 2027-10-25.

If you have questions or need clarifications, contact the product lead or the engineering owners listed above.
